BiblicalUsage: Hozai is named once, as the writer of the record of Manasseh's prayer and repentance. Nothing else is said about him, and his words are not quoted. His name survives because he kept the account of a king who turned back to God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Hozai matters because someone had to write down that Manasseh prayed. A king's repentance is only known because a recorder kept it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
